# Recreation Prompt

Create a browser-native, mobile-first portrait canvas game titled **Black Flame Block Party**. Preserve a grid exploration/card-survival loop: the player starts centered on a configurable square grid, taps the current or adjacent orthogonal square, draws a modal event card after movement, resolves HP/SAN resource effects, reveals a hidden goal through one good card, wins by stepping onto that revealed goal, and loses when either resource reaches zero.

Transform the presentation using this steering prompt: Hocus Pocus witchy Halloween party. A Hocus Pocus witchy Halloween party game with camp magic, mischievous sisters, candlelit folklore, playful spooky charm, cursed comedy, and festive autumn spectacle with mobile-first controls, touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, optimized on game start for portrait UI format, and the best-adapted mobile UX version targeting portrait aspect ratios in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

The focal identity is a glowing witch hat at a candlelit Halloween block party. The hidden exit is a black-flame candle. Good cards are enchanted cocoa, glitter hexes, and candle folklore clues. Bad cards are mischievous sister cackles, talking-cat roasts, and broom closet chaos. Use procedural CSS/canvas art for a moonlit manor, cauldron glow, bats, lanterns, candle-grid tiles, pumpkins, spell particles, and mobile-readable HUD panels.

# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: Mobile-first canvas grid exploration / event-card survival game.
- objective: Move through a 5x5 grid, reveal a hidden goal with a special good card, and reach that revealed goal before either resource reaches zero.
- input model: Pointer/touch tap on the canvas; only the current tile or orthogonally adjacent tiles are actionable during PLAY state. UI buttons use native click/tap.
- core loop: Start from center tile, tap a legal square, mark it visited, draw a random card, resolve good/bad/neutral effects, update HP/SAN and logs, continue until win/fail.
- fail/friction state: Bad cards reduce HP or SAN; HP <= 0 or SAN <= 0 ends the run. The card modal temporarily blocks movement until resolved.

## Protected mechanics
- Configurable grid size defaults to 5 and spawns the player in the center.
- Hidden exit is randomized away from the spawn and must be revealed by the map/candle-style card before it can be won.
- Player can only move to same tile or one orthogonal neighbor while gameState is PLAY.
- Movement immediately opens a card event unless it enters the revealed exit.
- Card probability bands remain neutral 40%, bad 30%, good 30%.
- Good cards heal SAN, reveal nearby tiles, or reveal exit; bad cards damage HP/SAN; neutral card has no resource change.
- HP and SAN start at 100 and preserve the <= 0 failure semantics.
- Win, fail, restart, HUD update, log update, feedback strip, and card overlay state flow are preserved.

## Remixed target
Black Flame Block Party reframes the same grid-card survival loop as a campy witchy Halloween party: the player is a mobile-readable witch hat hopping between candle squares, mischievous sisters and sarcastic familiars are bad-card pressure, enchanted cocoa/glitter/candle clues are rewards, and the hidden exit becomes the black-flame candle. The scene, HUD, focal actor, procedural props, and copy are rebuilt in a Hocus Pocus-inspired folklore-party identity while preserving core mechanics.
